item.title: The AI Escalation Danger Trump and Xi Must Address
item.description: As Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Beijing on May 14–15 to discuss the future of U.S.-China AI cooperation, concerns are growing over escalatory tendencies in models like DeepSeek. Common AI benchmarking may offer a path toward safer development.

item.title: What May 15 Means for Somalia’s Federal Architecture and Global Shipping
item.description: New reports of piracy off Somalia’s coast are grabbing headlines, but the bigger story is a looming constitutional crisis on May 15 that poses a long-term risk to the country’s federal legitimacy, regional stability, and, ultimately, to global shipping lanes.

item.title: A Confident Beijing Welcomes President Trump
item.description: Scott Kennedy lays out how China’s leaders are approaching the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, and why China feels remarkably more confident compared to the first such summit in 2017.

item.title: The U.S.-China Trade Truce Has Not Solved the Gallium Problem
item.description: The upcoming Trump-Xi summit offers an opportunity to press Beijing on its commitments on critical minerals.

item.title: The Deal of the ART: Assessing the “America First” Trade Policy in Asia
item.description: Countries in Asia, especially Southeast Asia, have a lot riding on how U.S.-China trade issues are ultimately resolved.

item.title: Another Crack in the Tariff Wall
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch analyzes the Court of International Trade's recent ruling to invalidate the Trump administration's 10 percent tariffs.

item.title: Building the AI Workforce: The Math Behind the Pipeline
item.description: As AI reshapes work and innovation, mathematics is an essential infrastructure for both building advanced AI systems and effectively using them across the economy. Yet declining U.S. math performance threatens the talent pipeline needed to sustain U.S. competitiveness.

item.title: Japan’s New Defense Export Policy: Will Industry Seize the Day?
item.description: Japan’s historic relaxation of its defense export restrictions opens the door for its defense industry to expand globally. Still, success will require a sustained whole-of-government effort in collaboration with firms.

item.title: Keeping Score: Vietnam’s Spratly Island Overhaul Continues
item.description: Vietnam builds specialized infrastructure on its outposts.
